sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Advocacy intiatives with Women with Disabilities on SGBV

Partner in Uganda and CREA provided capacity strengthening for 20 girls and women with disabilities in 2022 with the objective of sharing knowledge on: 1. their roles and responsibilities in feminist movement and ending GBV and SGBV in their communities; 2. how to increase their power influence in the community where patriarchy is order of the day; 3. selfcare, collective wellness and healing for women leaders and rights activists. During a follow-up engagement with those same women and girls, they presented updates on what they have done since the first training carried out by CREA in Kampala. These included but were not limited to: 1-sensitization meetings, 2-radio talkshows, 3-counselling and guidance to survivors of violence, 4-training other leaders of women with disabilities, 5-additionally the partner organized an advocacy/consultative meeting with Women's Rights Organizations (with 21 participants). The objectives of the meeting were to bring on board issues of Girls and Women with Disabilities to the WROs attention, advocate for inclusion/representation of Girls and Women with Disabilities in WROs networks/alliance and to create networks with WROs working with minority groups. The meeting created awareness on issues affecting inclusion of Girls and women with Disabilities. The participants embraced disability inclusion and are committed to mainstream issues of women with disabilities in their programmes.
